translations.title: What I Feel for You
translations.text:
What I feel for you is so difficult.

It is not roses opening in the air,

it is roses opening in water.


What I feel for you. This thing that rolls

or breaks with so many of your gestures

or that you shatter with your words

and then gather up again in a gesture

and that overwhelms me in the yellow hours

and leaves me with a sweet, folded thirst.


What I feel for you, so painful

as the poor light of the stars

that arrives in pain and weariness.


What I feel for you, and yet

that travels so far it sometimes does not reach you.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: If I Were to Die Tonight
translations.text:
If I were to die tonight

if I could die

if I were dying

if this fierce coupling

endless

fought over and merciless

an embrace without pity

a kiss without reprieve

were to reach its height and loosen

if right now

if now

with my eyes half closed I were to die

were to feel it was over

that the striving had ceased

and the light were no longer a sheaf of swords

and the air were no longer a sheaf of swords

and others’ pain and love and living

and everything were no longer a sheaf of swords

and it ended with me

for me

forever

and it no longer hurt

and it no longer hurt
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Sea Is Nothing but a Well
translations.text:
The sea is nothing but a well of dark water,

the stars are only shining mud,

love, dream, glands, madness,

the night is not blue, it is yellow.


The stars are only shining mud,

the sea is nothing but a well of bitter water,

the night is not blue, it is yellow,

the night is not deep, it is cold and long.


The sea is nothing but a well of bitter water,

despite the verses men have written,

the sea is nothing but a well of dark water.


The night is not deep, it is cold and long;

despite the verses men have written,

love, dream, glands, madness.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Love
translations.text:
Love

from the shadow

from pain

love

I am calling you

from the suffocating well of memory

with nothing to sustain me or wait for you.

I am calling you

love

as one calls to fate

as one calls to sleep

to peace

I am calling you

with my voice

with my body

with my life

with all I have

and do not have

with desperation

with thirst

with tears

as if you were air

and I were drowning

as if you were light

and I were dying.

From a blind night

from forgetting

from hours shut tight

in solitude

without tears or love

I am calling you

as one calls to death

love

as one calls to death.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Noon
translations.text:
The air transparent, transparent

the sickle of morning,

the warm white mountains, the gestures of the waves,

all that sea, all that sea fulfilling

its profound task,

the sea lost in itself,

the sea, at that honeyed hour when instinct

hums like a drowsy bee…

Sun, love, lilies expanded, sea lilies,

Blond branches, tender and sensitive as bodies,

vast pale sands.


The air transparent, transparent

voices, silence.

On the shores of love, of the sea, of morning,

on the hot sand, trembling with whiteness,

each is a fruit ripening toward death.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: You Are Alone, All the Same
translations.text:
You are alone, all the same.

I do not touch your life, your loneliness, your brow,

I am in your night no more than a lake, a cup,

no more than a deep lake

from which you can drink even with eyes closed,

forgotten.

I am for you like another darkness, another night,

a foretaste of death,

what a man waits for on a cold day, waits for,

and it comes and he gives himself to night, to a mouth,

and total oblivion blinds and stuns him.


Boundless night,

pure, wakeful, alone,

solicitous of love, angel of every gesture…


You are alone, all the same.

Drunk, lucid, blue, your soul forgotten,

give yourself to the hour.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: No Longer
translations.text:
It will no longer be

no longer

we will not live together

I will not raise your child

I will not sew your clothes

I will not have you at night

I will not kiss you as I leave

you will never know who I was

why others loved me.


I will never find out

why or how, never

nor whether it was true

what you said I was

nor who you were

nor what I was to you

nor what it would have been like

to live together

to love each other

to wait for each other

to be.


I am nothing now but myself

forever, and you

will no longer

be anything to me but yourself. You are no longer here

in some future day

I will not know where you live

with whom

nor whether you remember me.

You will never hold me

as you did that night

ever.


I will never touch you again.


I will not see you die.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: This Limitation, This Barrier…
translations.text:
This limitation, this barrier

this separation

this loneliness, consciousness

fleeting, gratuitous, closed

self-absorbed consciousness

this consciousness

existing, naming itself

flashing for an instant

in absolute nothingness

in absolute night

in the void.


This loneliness

this vanity, consciousness

condemned, powerless

ending in itself

coming to an end

confined

in light

and yet rising up

growing vain

blinding itself

covering the void with curtains of smoke

flailing at illusions

and never touching anything

never knowing anything

never possessing anything.

This absence, distance

this confinement

this desperate

this vain, infinite loneliness

consciousness.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Who Are They, Who Are They
translations.text:
Who are they, who are they

inside my life

imposing tenderness

ghosts like me

momentary and vain

like leaves rotted each autumn

and leaving no memory.

Who are they, who are they.

They are these and no others

from before, from after

fruits of death

unavoidably, inevitably

inevitably

before or after

dead

so briefly warm, breathing and upright

and loving

why not

loving without fear

never joining

the other soul, the other body

the other fleeting life.

Who are they, who are they.

What brood of dead for the ground they tread

what earth among earth tomorrow

and today within me

what earthbound ghosts compelling my love.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: When I Buy a Mirror for the Bathroom
translations.text:
When I buy a mirror for the bathroom

I’ll look at my face

I’ll look at myself

for what other way is there, tell me

what other way to know who I am.

Whenever I lift my head

from the jumble of books and pages

and carry it, hollow and stuffed full

and let it rest there for a moment

I’ll look it in the eyes with a little

anxiety, curiosity, fear

or only with weariness, with boredom

with the old familiarity that belongs

or look at myself attentively, seriously

as that strange time—when I was eleven—

and say to myself, look, there you are

surely

I’ll think I don’t like it, or I’ll think

that face was the only one possible

and I’ll tell myself that’s me, that’s Idea

and smile at myself, giving myself courage.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: I Want to Die
translations.text:
I want to die. I don’t want to hear any more bells.

The night comes undone, silence cracks.

If now a somber choir in an impossible low register,

if an impossible organ were to descend to where I am.


I want to die, and then it shouts at me: you are dying,

I want to close my eyes because I am so tired.

If there is no gaze, no gift to sustain me,

if they turn away, if they take, what do I expect from night.


I want to die now, as the flowers freeze,

while the silent stars labor in vain,

while the stopped clock does not torment the silence.


I want to die. I do not die.


I do not die. Perhaps

so many, so many collapses, so many deaths, perhaps,

so much forgetting, rejection,

so many gods who fled with cherished words

will not let me die for good.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: From Everywhere They Come…
translations.text:
From everywhere they come,

blood and courage,

to save their land

the Orientals;

they come from the hills,

with lance and saber;

amid the grasses they emerge,

the Orientals.


They leave the towns,

out of the woods they come,

at every corner they wait,

the Orientals.


Because they left their lives,

their friends and possessions,

because dearer to them

is the freedom they do not have,

because the land is another’s

and freedom another’s,

and because peoples always

know how to break their chains.


There were ten, there were twenty,

there were fifty,

there were a thousand, thousands,

now they cannot be counted.


Rebellious and brave

they march away,

leaving behind

the things they love most.


Like a sweeping wind

they sweep everything along,

like cleansing water

they come to wash it clean.


Because they left their lives…
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Bodies Laid Out, Bodies…
translations.text:
Bodies laid out, bodies

endless, tangible, forgetting the cold

that will slowly flood and fill them.


Golden bodies, arms, knotted warmth

forgetting the shadow now trembling,

still, expectant, ready to emerge

that shields blind skin.


Forgotten too, the white bones

that affirm each life is no dream,

truer to form than skin,

than blood, changeable, momentary.


Bodies laid out, bodies

submissive, happy, tangible,

endless…


Joyful children emerge, wet and fragrant,

victorious young people, upright as their instinct,

women at the summit of sweetness,

they lie down, rise, speak,

their mouth speaks, one day scattered,

they rise, look at one another with the gaze of the eternal.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Letter II
translations.text:
You are far away, to the south;

there it is not yet four.


Reclining in your chair,

leaning on the table in the café

of your room,

stretched out on a bed,

yours or someone else’s

who I wish I could erase

—I am thinking of you, not of those who seek

at your side what I want as well—.

I have been thinking of you for an hour

perhaps half an hour,

I don’t know.


When the light runs out

I’ll know it is nine;

I’ll smooth the bedspread,

put on my black dress

and run a comb through my hair.


I’ll go to dinner,

of course.


But at some point

I’ll come back to this room,

throw myself on the bed,

and then your memory—

what am I saying—

my desire to see you,

for you to look at me,

your presence as a man missing from my life

will become,

as now you become in the evening

that is already night,

the sole and only thing

that matters to me in the world.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Keeping Silent
translations.text:
I am trembling

the bare tree is trembling and, in mirrors,

singing

and the moon is singing

laughing

without silences

the lyrical and romantic

flute and sickle in the sky

for the first time

open their cherry light and dung.


Neither mornings can complain

nor the burning torpor that, for its barrenness,

I sing no more, I sing no more

nor can I undo spring

nor deny it and drink

nor kill without meaning to

nor walk by touch

since the air is hard

and coins, madnesses

wait

for the mark of water

in distress, laughing

laughing, laughing.


Ah, if rancor, if then

I no longer want

I could no longer, it passes, never reaches

a wave wanders, the tide

loses its bearings like this

and the sun exists here only in words

But in the sky

there is room for many, so many. Sometimes

they bother each other, bite

at the lips.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Letter I
translations.text:
As I move about the house

saying darling to you

with a fervent voice

with desperation

that this poor word

may not be enough to caress you

or sacrifice something

or give my life for you

darling

to summon you

to do something for this

for this invalid love.

And that is all,

darling.

I say darling and see

your eyes still pressed to mine

as if bound by love

looking at me, looking at me

while we made love

your eyes looking at me

your whole face

you

and it was life or death

to be like that

looking at each other.

And I close the windows saying

darling

darling, and I don’t care

that you are thinking of something else

and no longer even remember.

I am stopped

in that gaze of yours

in that look of yours

in our love, looking at each other

and I wander through the house

turning off the lights

putting away the dresses

thinking of you

looking at you

not letting you fall

yearning for you

loving you

saying darling.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Perhaps It Was Not Thinking
translations.text:
Perhaps it was not thinking, the formula, the secret,

but giving and taking, lost, ingenuously,

perhaps I could have chosen, or necessarily

had to ask meaning of everything.


Perhaps living was not this silent

and mercilessly standing at the edge of anguish

and stubbornly feeling beneath its music

a silence of death, an abyss in everything.


Perhaps I should have stayed with quiet loves

that could fill my life with a name

instead of seeking the man who had escaped,

stripped bare, soulless, pure, a skeleton.


Perhaps it was not thinking, the formula, the secret,

but loving oneself and loving, lost, ingenuously.


Perhaps I could have risen like a burning flower

or had a seed’s profound destiny

instead of this terrible yellow lucidity

and standing like a statue with empty eyes.


Perhaps I could have bent this fate of mine

into ineffable music. Or necessarily…
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Sun, the Sun, Its Glow…
translations.text:
The sun, the sun, its glow

its affectionate care

its courage, its grace, its warm smell

its height

at midday

falling and climbing through the dark of the sky

staggering, golden

like a pure drunkard.


Days upon days, nights, seasons

to live like this, to die

please, please

an outstretched hand

tears and alms

and help and favors

and pity and gifts.


The dead tugging at the heart.

Life pushing them away

kicking them hard

kicking them brutally.


Everything crucified and corrupted

and rotten to the marrow

everything rickety, impure, in pieces

utterly finished

waiting now for what

days upon days.


And the sun, the sun

its flight

its heavenly idleness

its work as lover, as idler

its passion

its endless love

its yellow gaze

falling and flooding the purity of the sky

like a burning drunkard

like an ignited corpse

like a madman blinded at midday.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: When a Soft Mouth, a Sleeping Mouth, Kisses…
translations.text:
When a soft mouth, a sleeping mouth, kisses

as if dying then,

sometimes, when it goes beyond the lips

and the eyelids fall, filled with desire,

as silently as the air allows,

the skin with its silky warmth asks for nights

and the kissed mouth

in its ineffable joy asks for nights, too.


Ah, silent nights, of soft dark moons,

long, sumptuous nights, crossed by doves,

in air made of hands, of love, of given tenderness,

nights like ships…


It is then, in the height of passion, that the one who kisses

knows, ah, too much, without reprieve, and sees that now

the world becomes a distant miracle,

that deep summers open their lips to him,

that his consciousness abdicates,

that at last he is himself, forgotten in the kiss

and a passionate wind bares his temples,

it is then, in the kiss, that eyelids descend,

and the air trembles with a trace of life,

and what is not air trembles too: the burning sheaf of hair,

the velvet now of the voice, and, sometimes,

the illusion already inhabited by deaths held in suspension.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: If I Am Standing
translations.text:
If I am standing

alone in the snow

it is logical

that I should be a clock


how else would eternity

find its way?
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Over There at the Table…
translations.text:
Over there on the table

are my hands

Below, on the floor

are my feet

Outside

far away somewhere

I do not see

what you see

with my eyes
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Text
translations.text:
I see the weightless clouds

I see the weightless sun

I see how easily they draw

an endless process

as if they trusted

in me, here on earth

as if they knew that I

am their words
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Nude Maja
translations.text:
I lean tenderly on the night

with the help of a rusted balustrade

I find the path to my cheek and shoulder

I find the path to my tenderness

iron and flesh.

The rest are flags waving silently

questioning outside and within

in the space of night, in the space of the soul:

death?

I place my hand on the throbbing face

of night

I brush a little rust from my cheek.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Inside the First Factory There Is a Second…
translations.text:
Inside the first factory there is a second,

inside the second there is a third,

inside the third a fourth factory, and so on.


Inside factory no. 3517 there is a man beside a machine


In factory no. 1423 there is a man beside a machine


Man no. 8611 has been raving about freedom all this time


At the end of all the factories assembled there is a man making money
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: I Have No Desire for More Scenery…
translations.text:
“I” have no desire for more scenery

“I” have no desire for more anecdotes

about painted mountains

“I” do not want to see more universes emerge

within the limits of what is reasonable

“I” do not want to hear more fire alarms

every time the sun comes up

“I” do not want to pretend I am dead

I am afraid

This is a critique of all “poetics”

because it is a critique of fear in the face of factual powerlessness
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Stone on the Beach Evaporates…
translations.text:
The stone on the beach evaporates.

The lake perishes beneath the sun.

The animals’ skeletons

lie hidden beneath the eternal sands

of the desert.

Things walk,

die into one another,

sail like thoughts

in the soul of space.

Caravans of living sand.


Is this a threat?

Where is my heart?

Prisoner in the stone.

Hidden in a lake.

Beating deep inside

a humped camel,

lying in the sand

groaning as it goes to die.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Stage
translations.text:
There are tapestries with scenes of war

hung all along the Maginot Line

meticulous prints of the Invincible Armada

float on every sea in the world

While Potemkin on the front page of Izvestia

is shipwrecked on a Pacific island

Or statues: Ivan the Terrible

smiles at the sight of Harlem

de Gaulle rides into Wenceslas Square

at the head of the Red Army

and enormous modern sculptures: the Great Wall of China

between Spain and Spain

while Napoleon dies in Formosa
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Stage
translations.text:
What is written is always something else

And what is described is something else again

Between the two lies the undescribed

which, as soon as it is described,

opens new undescribed territories

It is indescribable

Though darkness is defined by light

and light by darkness

something always remains outside.

And though this remainder “is defined”

as gardens laid waste

behind the growing iron railings

something always remains: logic

But though logic is not defined

but hidden beneath layers of gardens

painted from garden to garden

there always remains an unease

a desperation

a pulse without a body

This is a critique of the body

because it is a critique of life.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: When the Map of the Stage Is Incorporated…
translations.text:
When the map of the stage is incorporated

into the map of what lies beyond the stage

When the word has settled into the thing

and is objectively conditioned by the order of things


When language at last has sedimented

in the likeness, for example, of ancient minerals

and when style has clearly crystallized

in the likeness, for example, of transparent quartz


When communication

(in the likeness, for example, of the words used:

incorporated, settled, sedimented, crystallized)

is caught in a trap


then choice, dreams, history must

(in the likeness, for example, of dark utopias)

write themselves between the lines

(in the likeness, for example, of the youngest guerrilla)
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Then They Grow Grain on an Altar in Chile…
translations.text:
Then they grow grain on an altar in Chile

Then they pour milk into an old cannon

Then they pile firewood from poisoned arrows

Then they plant rice in an abandoned bastion


Then they play hide-and-seek in an empty parliament

Then they play ball with innocent bombs

Then they play chess with tiny pieces

of what was once a great president


Then they grow wine on stony Mafia soil

Then they sacrifice goats and lambs at a bank

Then they drive around Sofia in a Rolls-Royce

Then they burn rubles and dollars and francs


Then they sing songs about the happiness of peoples

Then they sing songs about the grief of peoples

Then they sweep all the parties away like a gale

and bring down the castle of the last paper tiger.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: There Are Warehouses of Surplus Corn, Artichokes, and Wheat…
translations.text:
There are warehouses of surplus corn, artichokes, and wheat

that will never be sold for a small profit

There are pigs fattened to sickness

fed artificially to give them a healthy appetite


There are heaps of rice and worm-eaten tomatoes

and mountains of stinking, rotting meat

There are ministers of agriculture and grim prelates

who consider themselves unaccountable for the misery of the hungry


There is enough fish for everyone, enough protein

There are fish filling the nets of the hungry

There are fish for the throbbing social machinery

that only makes the well-fed even more sated


There are people who have long had brilliant knowledge

of the common sense of a fair distribution of profits

Yet they believe the friendship of peoples

can live on exploitation, speeches, and air.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The Bed of Thorns
translations.text:
In my bed by night I sought him

whom my soul loves; I sought him, but did not

find him (Song of Songs III)

In my bed of flowers

my lips love him;

they do not love him, no,


they only dream of him.

If Love does not come,

I would die.

If Love

does not come—

I will die.


My arms seek him,

my moan calls him: “Where are you, Beloved,


a little bundle of myrrh?

Tell me, please,

if you want me to come.

There is

no sleep in my eyes

when your arm does not hold me,

when you

leave;

joy is far away.

I will go looking for you,

like a wounded

doe

that seeks the spring,

the spring of living water.”

I come upon the

soldiers

guarding the town: “Have you not seen

the Love of my

life?”

They have taken my cloak,

the cloak of a widow,

and with their cruel

hands

they have struck me senseless;

yet, ah, their blows

hardly hurt,

for what takes away the pain

is a gentler wound.

A little farther on

I hear a moan.


I see him on the Cross,

where he dies calling to me,

hands and feet nailed,


his head among thorns.

His moans

I understood well.


If Love does not come

I would die.

If Love does not come,

I will

die.

When I see him die,

my heart sighs;

I embrace the

Cross

as one embraces a vine trunk.

“Jesus, I no longer want

the bed that once

pleased me;

I made it of flowers,

and you want it of thorns;

if you want me in

yours,

I would sleep in it,

hands and feet nailed,


head among thorns,

and a lance thrust in my heart

to take my

life.”


Version by José Batlló
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied source text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: What Do You Thank Me For, Father, by Accompanying Me…
translations.text:
What do you thank me for, Father, by accompanying me

with this trust

that your death has created between us?


You cannot give me anything. I cannot give you anything,

and that is why you understand me.

translations.title: Though You No Longer Sleep with Me…
translations.text:
Though you no longer sleep

with me at night,

only chance will tell us

whether it is final.


For though pleasure will never again

be the same,

in life, forgettings

rarely last.

translations.title: Final Song
translations.text:
Paper roses are not real

and they burn

just like a thoughtful brow

or the touch of a sheet of ice.


Paper roses are, in truth,

too aflame for the heart.

translations.title: She Lived in a Bordered Country…
translations.text:
She lived in a country bounded

by the nearby coast of death

and the garden of childhood, which she never forgot.


Hers was a more innocent world.

Mysterious, because simple,

like a sundial.

translations.title: Resolve
translations.text:
Resolve to be happy

above all, against everyone

and against myself again

—above all, to be happy—

I return to that resolve.

But longer lasting than the will to mend

is the heart’s pain.

translations.title: At Night…
translations.text:
At night,

when you descend.


But it is useless, I will never

return to where you

were already being born as a memory.


Perhaps the blood suddenly grows. The blood grows

to far beyond that arm.


No one but the unarmed hand,

the faint palm

and this pain.

translations.title: A Happy Life
translations.text:
In an old, inefficient country,

something like Spain between two

civil wars, in a town by the sea,

to own a house and a little land

and no memories. To read nothing,

to suffer nothing, write nothing, pay no bills,

and live like a ruined nobleman

amid the ruins of my intelligence.
